# Get started

> Install Paneflow, open a terminal pane, and run your first coding agent. Review its changes and keep its session running when you close the app.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow is a native terminal multiplexer for coding agents. Run Claude Code,
Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, or shell commands in separate panes, follow their
activity, and review their changes in one interface.

Paneflow is free and open source. It runs on **Linux** (x86_64 and ARM64),
**macOS** (Apple Silicon), and **Windows** (x86_64). You do not need Rust
to install it.

## Run your first agent

### Download and install Paneflow

Choose the download for your operating system, then follow its installation
guide. On macOS, you can also install with Homebrew.

### Download links

- [macOS Apple Silicon DMG](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v0.17.6/paneflow-0.17.6-aarch64-apple-darwin.dmg)
- [Linux x86_64 AppImage](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v0.17.6/paneflow-0.17.6-x86_64.AppImage)
- [Windows x86_64 MSI](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/download/v0.17.6/paneflow-0.17.6-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi)
- [All release artifacts and Linux ARM64](https://paneflow.dev/download)

Homebrew on macOS:

```bash
brew install --cask arthjean/paneflow/paneflow
```

Read the [Linux installation guide](/docs/installation/linux),
[macOS installation guide](/docs/installation/macos), or
[Windows installation guide](/docs/installation/windows). For other packages
or architectures, [compare installation formats](/docs/installation).

### Open Paneflow

Open Paneflow from your application launcher, Spotlight, the Applications
folder, or the Start menu. You can also run it from a terminal in your
project directory:

```Terminal
paneflow
```

On first launch, Paneflow opens a workspace with a terminal pane. You do not
need a Paneflow account or API key. Telemetry is off by default and only
enabled with your consent.

**Paneflow does not open?** Check the graphics requirements below and follow
the [troubleshooting guide](/docs/troubleshooting). If your terminal cannot
find `paneflow`, follow your operating system's installation guide to make
the command available.

### Split the terminal into panes

Use the default shortcuts to open a second pane and move between panes:

- `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D` - split horizontally.
- `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E` - split vertically.
- `Alt+Arrow` - move focus between panes.
- `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N` - open another workspace.

Use `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` on Linux and Windows. Each new pane opens
a shell in the same working directory.

### Start an installed agent

Install your agent separately and complete its setup before running it in
Paneflow. In a terminal pane, run **one** of these commands for the agent
you use:

```Claude Code
claude
```

```Codex
codex
```

```OpenCode
opencode
```

You can run other CLI agents or shell commands in any pane. Each agent uses
its own account and model provider. The activity status Paneflow shows
depends on the agent's integration.

To run a second agent alongside the first, start it in another pane.

## Review the changes

After an agent edits files, open **Changes** in the dock to review the
active checkout's diff against `HEAD`. It includes staged and unstaged
changes and untracked files. Open **Files** to read or edit files in the
integrated editor.

If tasks need separate working directories, use
[Git worktrees](/docs/worktrees).

## Keep sessions running

When quitting Paneflow, choose **Keep sessions running** to leave shells
and agents running. Reopen the app to reconnect to those sessions.

The machine and session host must stay running. A machine restart or host
crash ends those processes. Choose **Stop everything and quit** to end
the sessions when you exit.

## System requirements

| Platform | System | Graphics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | x86_64 or ARM64; see the [Linux installation guide](/docs/installation/linux) | Vulkan loader (`libvulkan1` / `vulkan-loader`) and a compatible GPU driver |
| macOS | macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple Silicon | Metal |
| Windows | Windows 10 (1809+) or 11, x86_64 | DirectX 11 |

On Windows, use PowerShell or Git Bash to let Paneflow track your current
working directory. `cmd.exe` does not report directory changes through the
OSC 7 sequence Paneflow uses.

## Install with an AI agent

To have a CLI agent help install Paneflow, copy the prompt below into its
conversation. It asks the agent to identify your operating system and
architecture, read the matching installation guide, and request your
confirmation before running commands or an installer.
